node.label: Richard J. Evans
node.description: A historian of modern Germany who has also defended historical knowledge in public. In Defence of History (1997) answers the writers who brought postmodernist epistemology into historical theory; he names Hayden White, Frank Ankersmit, Keith Jenkins, Patrick Joyce, Dominick LaCapra and Beverley Southgate. He wrote it because the standard textbooks were still Carr’s What Is History? and Elton’s The Practice of History, which he found inadequate. Its introduction accepts White’s point that historians can learn from outside scrutiny of how historical knowledge is made, while rejecting Joyce’s claim that historians must accept postmodernity as an inescapable condition. Death in Hamburg (1987) connects cholera with social inequality and civic government. He served as an expert witness on the falsification of history in the 2000 Irving libel trial, and The Coming of the Third Reich (2003) began his history of Nazi Germany.
